elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer (PB) on termination
elements.evidence: "PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, no liquidated damages or penalty in respect of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination"; the 300% figure is deleted.≥
"no liquidated damages or penalty in respect of Development Costs"

elements.element: An early-termination fee exists and is expressed as a monetary amount
elements.evidence: The redline removes any payment entirely: "no liquidated damages or penalty" — no fee is stated.

elements.element: That fee is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No cap or fee-period measure appears anywhere in the revised text.

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: No sole-liquidated-amount formulation is inserted; 14.4.2 still speaks of "the amounts specified as being payable upon a given termination in Section 14.2".

reasons: The preferred level is achieved on its face: the 300% of Development Costs termination payment is deleted and replaced with an express negation of any liquidated damages or penalty payable by PB.
The fallback is not met (and need not be, since the locked target is preferred): no early-termination fee, no 3-months'-fees cap, and no sole-liquidated-amount statement.
The edit is narrowly scoped to the single payment formula in p0750, so minimality is satisfied.

Intent is not preserved: the surviving verb phrase "PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, no liquidated damages or penalty" is internally incoherent — a payment obligation with a payment window but nothing payable — and should be recast as "PB will not be required to pay SFJ any liquidated damages or penalty in respect of Development Costs...".

Intent is further disturbed because the deleted amount was the stated consideration "in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results"; PB now appears to acquire the Trial Data Package for no consideration, an unrelated commercial term the redline should not silently rewrite.

A dangling mechanic remains in Section 14.4.2, which continues to operate on "the amounts specified as being payable upon a given termination in Section 14.2" even though no such amount now exists under 14.2.1.
